description:
We are a multidisciplinary team of young visionaries who bring together talent, creativity, art, science, and technology with one shared purpose: to transform extraordinary ideas into experiences that inspire, educate, and transcend boundaries.

We are united by an insatiable curiosity to explore the unknown, a passion for pushing the limits of what is possible, and the belief that great innovations emerge when diverse talents, knowledge, and perspectives come together.
summary:
ORBIT is an immersive, interactive 3D virtual space museum that brings the extraordinary stories of space exploration back to life.
Designed primarily for children and teenagers aged 10 to 18, as well as educators, families, and space enthusiasts, ORBIT addresses a fundamental challenge: although young people are fascinated by the universe, scientific information often feels complex, distant, and difficult to understand.
Inspired by NASA’s “Abandoned but Not Forgotten” challenge, ORBIT transforms real space mission data into immersive, exciting, and participatory educational experiences.
Through three-dimensional environments, historical reconstructions, and computer vision technology, visitors can explore the history of spaceflight by using their own body movements to interact with virtual objects, without touching the screen.
ORBIT’s first two featured missions are the Apollo 17 Lunar Roving Vehicle on the Moon and the Cassini spacecraft, which explored Saturn and its system of moons.
Visitors can discover these technologies, examine their components, explore reconstructed settings, and relive pivotal moments in space exploration.
More than a virtual museum, ORBIT is a digital time capsule that preserves the legacy of technologies that expanded our understanding of the universe.
Their missions may have ended, but their stories deserve to live forever.
details:
1. What does our project do?

ORBIT transforms scientific and historical information about space missions into immersive, interactive educational experiences.

Unlike traditional museums, where visitors primarily observe exhibits, ORBIT enables users to become active participants in space exploration.

Upon entering the platform, visitors discover a cosmos-inspired virtual museum. From there, they can access different exhibits, navigate three-dimensional environments, and learn the stories of technologies that marked milestones in the exploration of the universe.

The Apollo 17 Lunar Roving Vehicle — The Moon

Visitors can discover the lunar rover, examine its components, watch its deployment, and explore a reconstruction of the lunar landscape inspired by the Apollo 17 mission. This experience helps them understand how the vehicle expanded astronauts’ ability to travel across the lunar surface, carry instruments, and conduct scientific research.

Cassini — Saturn

The Cassini experience showcases one of NASA’s most extraordinary robotic exploration missions. Through interactive visualizations and scientific storytelling, visitors will discover the spacecraft’s engineering, its journey to Saturn, its observations of the planet and its moons, and the discoveries that transformed our understanding of the Saturnian system. The Cassini mission ended in 2017 with a controlled entry into Saturn’s atmosphere, leaving an invaluable scientific legacy.

Touchless Interaction

One of ORBIT’s distinctive features is its use of computer vision technology. With MediaPipe, the platform interprets movements captured by a webcam and converts them into interactive commands, allowing users to manipulate virtual objects without touching the screen. Depending on the features available in each exhibit, users can explore, discover, examine and virtually disassemble components, drive vehicles, and learn through active participation.

ORBIT transforms visitors from passive spectators into active explorers.

2. What are its benefits?

ORBIT combines science education, immersive technology, and historical preservation to offer a new way to learn about space exploration.

Active, Experiential Learning

Rather than relying exclusively on technical explanations, ORBIT enables learning through exploration, observation, interaction, and discovery.

Access to Scientific Knowledge

Complex concepts in engineering, physics, robotics, and planetary science are presented through visual explanations, three-dimensional reconstructions, and interactive storytelling.

Immersive, Touchless Interaction

Computer vision technology offers an intuitive way to interact with the museum through body movements captured by a standard webcam.

Inspiring Interest in STEM

By transforming scientific information into exciting experiences, ORBIT aims to spark children’s and teenagers’ interest in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics.

Preserving Space Heritage

ORBIT keeps the stories of pioneering technologies accessible even after their missions have ended.

A Memorable Educational Experience

The integration of scientific accuracy, visual design, interactivity, and emotional storytelling turns learning into an adventure of discovery.

3. What is its impact?

ORBIT aims to bridge the gap between scientific knowledge and the curiosity of new generations.

Its primary goal is educational: to make space exploration more understandable, engaging, and accessible to children and teenagers.

By enabling users to interact with historic technologies and explore reconstructed space mission environments, ORBIT seeks to stimulate curiosity, critical thinking, and interest in STEM fields.

The platform also contributes to the digital preservation and interpretation of space exploration heritage.

The Apollo 17 Lunar Roving Vehicle represents a milestone in human mobility on another world, while Cassini symbolizes the extraordinary advances of robotic exploration in the outer solar system.

Together, these missions demonstrate how engineering, scientific curiosity, and technological innovation have expanded our understanding of the universe.

In the long term, ORBIT is envisioned as a scalable educational platform capable of incorporating new missions, spacecraft, and scientific discoveries.

Our vision is to inspire the next generation of explorers by allowing them to experience the achievements of those who made space exploration possible.

4. What tools, programming languages, hardware, or software did we use?

ORBIT integrates web development, interactive three-dimensional environments, computer vision, scientific visualization, and audiovisual storytelling. Its main technological components include:

Computer Vision and Motion-Based Interaction

ORBIT uses MediaPipe to process visual information captured by a webcam and interpret certain hand or body movements as interactive commands. This allows visitors to manipulate virtual objects and interact with compatible experiences without touching the screen.

Interactive Three-Dimensional Environments

3D models and reconstructed environments allow visitors to examine spacecraft, observe their components, and experience selected mission activities.

Web Architecture

ORBIT is designed as a digital museum accessible through a web browser, reducing the need for specialized virtual reality equipment.

Scientific and Historical Information

The platform uses official NASA documentation, imagery, and scientific resources as references for its educational content and historical reconstructions. Its initial information sources relate to the Apollo 17 and Cassini–Huygens missions.

Educational Storytelling

Narration, interactive activities, and historical reconstructions transform technical information into understandable and engaging learning experiences.

Together, these technologies create an environment where education, exploration, and scientific discovery converge.

5. In what ways is our project creative?

ORBIT’s creativity lies in transforming the legacy of completed space missions into immersive learning experiences that users can actively explore.

1. A Virtual Time Capsule

ORBIT preserves the stories of historic space vehicles and probes, allowing new generations to rediscover their scientific and technological importance.

2. Touchless Interaction

Instead of limiting visitors to watching a screen, ORBIT uses computer vision to turn physical movements into digital interactions.

3. Historical Reconstruction

Visitors can experience selected moments from significant missions, such as the deployment and operation of the Apollo 17 lunar rover, and discover Cassini’s scientific story.

4. Emotionally Engaging Scientific Storytelling

ORBIT connects scientific advances with human curiosity, making space vehicles and probes the central characters in stories of discovery, innovation, and exploration.

Its creativity lies not only in the technology itself, but also in how that technology makes scientific knowledge more exciting, understandable, and meaningful.

ORBIT does more than display the history of space exploration. It invites visitors to become part of its discovery.

6. What factors did our team consider?

During the design and development of ORBIT, our team considered six essential factors.

Target Audience

The experience is primarily intended for children and teenagers aged 10 to 18, while also welcoming teachers, families, and space exploration enthusiasts.

Scientific and Historical Accuracy

The project prioritizes reliable information and official NASA resources to accurately represent missions, technologies, and scientific discoveries.

Immersive Interactivity

ORBIT encourages active exploration and touchless interaction, allowing users to participate through movements recognized by computer vision technology.

Accessibility

The platform is designed for use on a computer, with the aim of bringing space heritage to people who cannot visit specialized physical museums.

Visual and Narrative Design

Scientific knowledge is presented through three-dimensional environments, cinematic storytelling, and interactive educational activities designed to capture attention and evoke emotion.

Scalability

ORBIT is designed to incorporate new exhibits and missions in the future, progressively expanding its educational possibilities.

These principles guide the project’s purpose: to integrate technology, scientific knowledge, and creativity to build meaningful learning experiences.

CONCLUSION

ORBIT is much more than an interactive space museum.

It is a bridge between the extraordinary achievements of the past and the explorers of tomorrow.

Through immersive experiences, real NASA mission information, and computer vision technology, ORBIT transforms scientific knowledge into opportunities for discovery.

From the lunar vehicle that expanded human exploration of the Moon to the Cassini spacecraft that revealed the wonders of Saturn, ORBIT celebrates the technologies and stories that transformed our understanding of the universe.

We may never be able to bring these spacecraft back to Earth.

But we can bring their stories to a new generation.

ORBIT. They explored the unexplored.
